A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIPMem study and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A.1–A.9. All 24 pages were compared; the scientific text, equations, figures, tables and appendices match.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments measuring memorization and downstream accuracy, including caption augmentation, embedding noise, sample removal, model-size comparisons and BLIP evaluation in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the memorization measurements and downstream accuracy experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The CLIPMem computation and mitigation procedures using multiple captions, text-embedding noise and memorized-sample removal are identical in Sections 3 and 4.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COCO, CC3M and YFCC100M training, ImageNet evaluation and the CIFAR-10 supervised control. The caption-poisoning and single-pass training scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SSLMem, supervised and DINO models, and random-removal and CLIP-similarity filtering baselines. No comparator is added, removed or revised in the main text or appendices.

E3.justification: The four-subset memorization evaluation, dataset sizes, training budgets, model configurations, metrics and caption-selection procedures remain identical, including the settings in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same caption and noise sensitivity studies, poisoning and sample-removal analyses, model-size comparison, neuron analyses and memorized-example case studies. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The same uncertainty values and plotted error bars appear in both versions. No information about seeds, repeated runs, confidence intervals or statistical tests is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and Figures 1–19 retain the same results and findings. For example, Table 5 reports ViT-Base CLIPMem of 0.438 and ImageNet linear-probing accuracy of 63.11% ± 0.91% in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, alignment and CLIPMem definitions in Equations 3–4, and normalization procedure in Appendix A.2 are identical. No formal assumption, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about CLIPMem, the text encoder's role in memorization, and mitigating memorization while improving downstream generalization.

C2.justification: The explanations distinguishing mis-captioned from atypical samples, interpreting modality and neuron effects, and discussing applicability remain unchanged throughout Section 4 and the appendices.

D1.justification: Hardware and training details in Appendix A.2, caption-generation code in Appendix A.8, and access references are unchanged. The added sponsor acknowledgement provides no new implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2, Appendix A.1 and the references are unchanged. The new funding acknowledgement does not alter the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds a sentence acknowledging financial and in-kind sponsors, especially the OpenAI Cybersecurity Grant, on page 10. It also updates the arXiv version/date stamp; scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement expands from two lines to three, slightly changing vertical spacing around the conclusion, acknowledgements and references on page 10. All figures, tables and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 makes sponsor credit more complete, but leaves the methods, evidence, analysis and reproducibility information unchanged. The slight page-10 reflow has no material effect on readability, so the revision does not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
